paragraphs: R’ Yose bar Bibi or Bibin.

Hyman cites Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 2:9 for Yose’s teaching that square tefillin are a law transmitted to Moshe at Sinai. In Shekalim 3:2, R’ Yose reports in the name of R’ Yose ben Pazi and R’ Yose bar Bibi in the name of R’ Shmuel. The Rabbis of Caesarea and R’ Yose bar Bibi report in the name of Shmuel. Hyman adds, “There Gamliel Zuga asked him,” referring to what he calls the Bavli reading.

Bereshit Rabbah 52:5 has R’ Yose ben Bibah saying, “The Lord is far from the wicked”—these are the prophets of the nations of the world. Vayikra Rabbah 11:8 has R’ Yishmael bar Bibi; Hyman suggests that the initials R-Y were written and became R’ Yishmael.

notes.text: The checked Shekalim passage gives the cup-measure chain with Yose bar Beivin; its Gamliel Zuga question instead addresses Yose son of Bun. Hyman’s wording and his “Bavli version” qualification are retained as a source question. His proposed Yishmael-to-Yose correction remains his conjecture.

No new primary scalar was returned. Square tefillin as law transmitted to Moshe at Sinai is a conventional הל״מ expansion. The two reporting chains and the contrast between R-prime Shmuel and untitled Shmuel remain. Earlier inspected Shekalim instead addresses Yose son of Bun in Gamliel Zuga’s question; supplied him and Hyman’s Bavli-version qualification remain unresolved. This need not mean a separate Bavli tractate parallel: Shekalim’s printed recension may be intended. Bibi/Bibin/Bibah and older ביבי/ביכי editorial provenance remain separate. Hyman’s apparent initials-to-Yishmael explanation is a conjecture, not proved correction history.

Hyman prints Megillah 2:9 (vol. II, p. 720). The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 4:9 ascribes the square-tefillin teaching to R’ Yose ben Bevai, with “black” bracketed in that edition. The consulted Shekalim cup-measure passage reads Bibi in Mechon-Mamre and Bibin in the Venice and Guggenheimer digital witnesses. The later question by Gamliel Zuga names Yose son of Bun in these editions and in the consulted text paginated as Shekalim 9a. Hyman’s exact Bavli edition remains uncollated. Bereshit Rabbah 52:5 names Yose ben Bibah and Vayikra Rabbah 11:8 names Yishmael bar Bevai. The proposed explanation involving the initials R-Y is Hyman’s.
